question: In the description-based account of intensional anaphora by Keshet and Abney, what presupposition does a pronoun carry regarding its antecedent description, and what formal logic implements it?
support_excerpts:
We propose that a pronoun presupposes that its corresponding
antecedent description is instantiated in each world of the context set.

We implement our proposal via a new logic (building on work
by Keshet (2018) and Abney & Keshet (2022)) that we name Plural Intensional
Presuppositional predicate calculus (or PIP).

question: According to the categorization following TacoDepth, what is the distinction between independent and plug-in radar-camera depth completion methods?
support_excerpts:
Following TacoDepth (Wang et al. 2025), we categorize
radar–camera depth completion methods as independent or
plug-in. Independent methods directly predict metric depth
from radar and RGB, whereas plug-in methods additionally
relyonanauxiliarymonoculardepthmodel.
expected_answer: Independent methods directly predict metric depth from radar and RGB, whereas plug-in methods additionally rely on an auxiliary monocular depth model.

question: How does the evaluation framework measure LLM attachment styles using the ECR-R scale, and why was the ECBench benchmark developed to complement it?
support_excerpts:
For model evaluation, we present the ECR-R
items to each model individually and require responses within a ﬁxed set of options. We then
compute the mean scores for anxiety and avoidance and map them onto a two-dimensional attachment space.

The ECR-R characterize the attachment tendencies of LLMs, but lacks realistic interpersonal interaction contexts. We therefore introduce a dialogue benchmark called ECBench for evaluating
emotional companionship capabilities in realistic
interaction scenarios.
expected_answer: The framework presents ECR-R items to models within a fixed option set, computing mean anxiety and avoidance scores to map models into a 2D attachment space. Because ECR-R characterizes tendencies but lacks realistic interpersonal contexts, ECBench was introduced to evaluate emotional companionship capabilities in realistic dialogue.

question: How does V-JEPA adapt joint-embedding predictive architectures to video, and how does its relationship with MAE/V-MAE differ in terms of prediction targets?
support_excerpts:
V-JEPA extends the same idea to video by predicting representations of masked spatiotemporal regions from visible spatiotemporal context [5]. This places I-JEPA/V-JEPA close to MAE/V-MAE in masking structure, while
separating them by the prediction target.
expected_answer: V-JEPA extends joint-embedding prediction to video by predicting representations of masked spatiotemporal regions from visible context. While its masking structure is close to MAE/V-MAE, it differs by predicting learned representation targets rather than reconstructing low-level pixel details.

h≡ O h′, then any estimator ˆτmeasurable with respect to O assigns ˆτ(h) = ˆτ(h′), so at least one is

expected_answer: Two policies are observationally equivalent if they produce identical observable responses on all inputs in the observation support O. An estimator is guaranteed well-defined and correct if and only if all policy pairs with distinct target estimand values tau are observationally inequivalent, making tau constant on each equivalence class.
